terms.comment: The larger of the Baliārēs īnsulae (Lewis & Short s.v. Baliares). A large island takes a preposition, as a country does: in Baliārem Majōrem, in Baliārī Majōre.

evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Majori(c)a: Majori(c)a [ins.], Balearis major, Majorca

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
